speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Health what is the rationale for banning ex-offenders from donating blood within one year of their prison release.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: However, infections can only be detected some time after the blood donors have been infected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Therefore, donors who have been exposed to infection risks will be asked to defer their donation until after the window period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For this reason, the World Health Organization recommends an appropriate deferral period after ex-offenders have been released from prison before blood donation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I do understand we are following WHO guidelines.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But WHO says prisons are extremely high-risk environments for transmission of HIV due to over-crowding, poor nutrition, limited access to healthcare, continued drug use, unsafe injecting practices, unprotected sex and tattooing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This might be representative of other prisons, but can I ask the Senior Minister of State whether this is representative of the Singapore prisons?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And having myself visited the prisons, I am quite sure that this is not.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If it is not, then why do we follow the WHO guidelines when our prisons are not the same as other prisons?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The second clarification is, if we really do believe that the Singapore Prison is an area where there is high infections, then, surely, MOH should be doing something to protect our inmates against HIV, Hepatitis B which we can vaccinate against, and Hepatitis C, rather than the stigma of the ex-offender coming out and then, going to try and donate blood, and the doctor says, "No, you can't because you are an ex-offender." And that is a real-life example because it was an ex-offender who emailed me after coming to my blood donation drive in Nee Soon East and being turned away.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As I have mentioned, HSA has very high standards on donor criteria to ensure the safety of blood supply.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I think that this is something that all of us do support.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We also know that studies have shown that inmates of prisons and corrective institutions have a higher incidence of infections from blood-borne diseases such as Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We also acknowledge that they are considered a higher risk group compared to the population.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like I have mentioned in my reply, they may be in the window period, so therefore, we have adopted what WHO has recommended, taking into consideration all these factors.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: On this topic of blood donation, I mentioned it yesterday in my cut, too, that there are persons with mental health conditions who declared and were also turned away at the blood banks here in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: It just concerns me that between ex-offenders and persons with mental health conditions, our blood donation policy seems to be entrenched deeply in stigma that we are trying so hard to get rid of.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Senior Minister of State explain why persons with mental conditions are turned away at blood donation drives?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As far as I know, not all mental conditions will be excluded from blood donation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We are saying that a year from their release date, they have very high potential of being infected with Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C and HIV, surely, MOH should have a programme to help these inmates following their release.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I think we must be cognisant that the reason why they are inmates is because of certain things that have happened, prior to that.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: That actually pre-disposes them to some high-risk behaviours.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: While we do not want to say that every single person who has been admitted to prison is considered high risk, we do need to take an approach whereby we have to err on the side of caution.
